classification.difficultyReason: Solve a co-interior algebraic equation, evaluate two expressions and prove a second parallel pair by corresponding angles.

content.prompt: $AB$ is parallel to $CD$. Prove that $WY$ is parallel to $XZ$.

spec.description: Horizontal lines A–W–X–B and C–Y–Z–D have one right-pointing parallel mark each. Oblique segments WY and XZ have no parallel marks. Non-reflex sectors BXZ, WYZ and XZD carry 7a, 3(a + 10) and 5a respectively, without degree symbols. All regions remain unfilled.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel to CD. The upper and lower horizontal lines have collinear point orders A,W,X,B and C,Y,Z,D. The marked angles at X and Z are co-interior. The marked angles at Y and Z are corresponding for the two oblique lines. Coordinates reproduce schematic placement and are not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated values or parallel marks on WY and XZ.

answer.short: $WY\parallel XZ$, since $\angle WYZ=\angle XZD=75^\circ$ (equal corresponding angles).
answer.worked:
Since $AB\parallel CD$, co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}5a+7a&=180\\12a&=180\\a&=15\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\angle WYZ&=3(a+10)\\&=3(15+10)\\&=75^\circ\\\angle XZD&=5a\\&=5(15)\\&=75^\circ\end{align*}$$
Therefore $WY\parallel XZ$, because corresponding angles are equal.
